subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: If x = 3 cos t − 2 cos³t and y = 3 sin t − 2 sin³t, find dy/dx.

mark_split.label: Differentiate x with respect to t
Differentiate y with respect to t

The mathematics was checked independently before writing: the ratio of the two numerical derivatives matched cot t at t = 0.7 (1.18724183) and t = 1.3 (0.27761565), two values chosen on either side of π/4 so that cos 2t changes sign between them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what common factor comes out of each derivative, and what cancels when you divide.

steps.label: State the parametric rule
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write the rule before differentiating. Both curves are given through the parameter t, so t is the variable everything is differentiated with respect to.
lines: Given x = 3 cos t − 2 cos³t  and  y = 3 sin t − 2 sin³t
x and y are both given in terms of the parameter t, so

recall.must_convey: That for a parametric pair, dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt).
accept: dy by dx is dy by dt divided by dx by dt
differentiate both with respect to t and divide
state the parametric rule first
parametric form kabatti dy by dt by dx by dt teesukovali
t is the parameter so both derivatives are in t
find dx by dt and dy by dt separately

steps.why: Neither equation gives y in terms of x, so dy/dx cannot be found directly. Dividing the two derivatives with respect to t removes the parameter and leaves the slope.
common_mistakes: Writing dy/dx = (dx/dt)/(dy/dt), which is the reciprocal of the correct rule.
Trying to eliminate t between the two equations first, which is much longer here.
steps.memory_tip: Both parts have the same shape, 3 × (function) − 2 × (function cubed), so expect the two derivatives to have the same shape too.

steps.label: Differentiate x with respect to t
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Take 3 sin t out as a common factor, then use 2cos²t − 1 = cos 2t. The examiner looks for the double angle form, because that is the factor which cancels later.

recall.must_convey: That dx/dt = 3 sin t cos 2t, using cos 2t = 2cos²t − 1.
accept: differentiate cos cubed t by the chain rule to get minus three cos squared t sin t
take three sin t common
two cos squared t minus one is cos two t
three sin t common teesi cos two t rayali
dx by dt is three sin t cos two t
the bracket becomes the double angle cosine

steps.why: Both terms carry a factor sin t, so taking it out leaves the bracket 2cos²t − 1, which is one of the standard forms of cos 2t. Writing it as cos 2t is what makes the cancellation in the last step visible.
common_mistakes: Differentiating cos³t as 3cos²t and forgetting the inner derivative −sin t.
Losing the sign, so the bracket comes out as 1 − 2cos²t instead of 2cos²t − 1.
steps.memory_tip: cos 2t has three standard forms. The one with cosines only, 2cos²t − 1, is the one that appears when x is differentiated.

steps.label: Differentiate y with respect to t
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Here the common factor is 3 cos t and the bracket is 1 − 2sin²t, which is the same cos 2t written the other way. Both derivatives must end with the SAME factor for the question to work out.

recall.must_convey: That dy/dt = 3 cos t cos 2t, using cos 2t = 1 − 2sin²t.
accept: differentiate sin cubed t to get three sin squared t cos t
take three cos t common
one minus two sin squared t is cos two t
three cos t common teesi cos two t vasthundi
dy by dt is three cos t cos two t
the same double angle factor appears again

steps.why: The inner derivative of sin³t is cos t, so both terms carry cos t and it factors out. The bracket 1 − 2sin²t is cos 2t written in sines, the same quantity that came out of dx/dt.
common_mistakes: Writing the bracket as 2sin²t − 1, which is −cos 2t and flips the sign of the answer.
Differentiating sin³t as 3sin²t without the inner cos t.
steps.memory_tip: Two of the three cos 2t forms are used in this question — the cosine one for x, the sine one for y. Both are the same number.

steps.label: Divide and cancel cos 2t
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos 2t is a common factor of both derivatives and cancels. Valid where dx/dt ≠ 0, that is where sin t ≠ 0 and cos 2t ≠ 0.
lines: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) = (3 cos t cos 2t)/(3 sin t cos 2t)
The 3 and the factor cos 2t cancel, leaving cos t/sin t

recall.must_convey: That cos 2t cancels between the two derivatives, leaving dy/dx = cot t.
accept: cos two t cancels top and bottom
the answer is cot t
cos t by sin t is cot t
cos two t cancel ayipoyi cot t migulutundi
divide three cos t cos two t by three sin t cos two t
only the ratio of cos t to sin t is left

steps.why: Both derivatives were deliberately written with cos 2t as a factor, so the division is one cancellation rather than a page of trigonometric simplification. Without that factoring the ratio does not reduce.
common_mistakes: Expanding everything into powers of sin t and cos t instead of factoring, so nothing cancels.
Writing tan t by dividing dx/dt by dy/dt.
steps.memory_tip: Factor first, divide second. The cos 2t was put in front on purpose so that one cancellation finishes the question.
